topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and presents the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Foundational Etiology: Genetics, Bad Luck, and Epidemiological Variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the broad conceptual frameworks of cancer etiology, contrasting endogenous replication errors and genetic predispositions with environmental exposures and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the oncogenic mechanisms of biological pathogens, focusing on viruses and bacteria with a detailed case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Metabolic Activation and DNA Adducts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific physical agents and chemical mutagens undergo xenobiotic metabolism to form reactive species and cause direct DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, including chronic inflammation, the two-stage initiator-promoter model, and age- or tissue-specific host susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental methods used to determine whether exposures cause cancer.
